note: Game balance values chosen by our team for gameplay. Not NASA data except where a source is named. First-guess numbers: tune them while playtesting.

oxygen.label: Oxygen
oxygen.source: Daily use based on NASA life-support planning values (about 0.8 kg per person per day). Verify before presenting.

water.label: Water
water.source: Daily use based on NASA's minimum drinking water value (2.5 L per person per day). Recovery is a game number.

power.label: Power
power.source: Game number. Unused power is lost at the end of the day.

manual.note: Per O circle tapped (splitting water with electricity). Game numbers. Water use follows the real ratio of about 1 kg water per 1 kg oxygen, rounded.

greenhouse.label: Greenhouse
greenhouse.note: Power Room sets the light: off = 0 plants can grow, low = 2, high = 4. Each plant costs water and gives food (per-plant values are the high level divided by 4).

power_room.label: Power Room
power_room.job: Player splits the daily power budget between rooms here.

radiation.rule: If sep.found_in_donki is true the sun sparks always arrive. Otherwise roll the random chance for the event level and tell the player it is a simplified rule.

on_empty.rule: When a resource reaches zero: lose a heart, show the explanation, refill one day so the player can fix the mistake.

messages.watch: The Sun just burst out a huge flash of energy! Invisible fast sun sparks may race to the Moon and could make Raed sick. Get the shelter ready. Its thick walls keep Raed safe!
messages.radiation_hit: Ouch! Fast sun sparks from the Sun reached the base and the crew was not in the shelter. Thick walls block most radiation, so astronauts hide there during a storm.
messages.radiation_blocked: Safe! The crew was in the shelter and the radiation was blocked.
messages.false_alarm: The sun sparks did not arrive this time. Preparing cost power, but being ready is what real astronauts do.
messages.oxygen_empty: Oxygen ran out! The air machines need electricity, so air comes first.
messages.water_empty: Water ran out! The greenhouse uses water, so watering plants can leave less to drink.
messages.food_empty: Food ran out! Plants need water, light and power to grow.
messages.lucky: The sun sparks did not arrive this time, so Raed was lucky! But nobody can be sure ahead of time, so real astronauts get ready anyway.
messages.dusty_note: Days are different: dust, sunshine and thirst change what Raed needs.
messages.too_slow: Too slow! The shelter was ready, but Raed did not get inside in time, and the radiation hurt.
messages.too_slow_lucky: Raed was too slow to reach the shelter, but luckily no sun sparks came this time. Next time, hurry!

fact_cards.oxygen: We breathe in oxygen to stay alive. The Moon has no air, so astronauts make and recycle their own. The machines need electricity to run!
fact_cards.water: Astronauts need clean water to drink and to grow plants. Water is precious in space, so they recycle as much as they can.
fact_cards.power: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. On the Moon, night lasts about two weeks! Power runs the air machines, the plants and the shelter, but there is never enough for everything.
fact_cards.food: Plants in the greenhouse can make fresh food, but they need water, light and power.
fact_cards.radiation: The Sun sometimes bursts out a flash of energy called a solar flare. Fast invisible sun sparks can follow it, and they can make astronauts sick. Thick walls stop most of them, so astronauts hide in a shelter. This game uses real solar flashes recorded by NASA.
fact_cards.shelter: A shelter with thick walls blocks most radiation, so astronauts hide there during a storm.
fact_cards.hearts: Hearts show how healthy the astronaut is. Keep air, water and food up, and stay safe from radiation.

credits.text: Real solar events from NASA's DONKI. Daily oxygen and water needs are based on NASA life-support planning values. All other numbers are simplified for the game.

days.title: A calm start
days.text: Everything is quiet on the Moon. Plan your first day!

days.title: Dusty panels
days.text: Moon dust covers the solar panels, so there is a little LESS power today.

days.title: Extra sunny
days.text: The Sun is shining bright, so there is a little MORE power today.

days.title: Thirsty day
days.text: Raed worked hard and drinks a bit more water today.

days.title: Last day!
days.text: Almost done! Make this day count.

molecule_facts: 💧 H₂O is the science name for water! H means hydrogen and O means oxygen. Every drop of water is made of tiny pieces like this one: 2 H and 1 O.
⚡ Electricity can split water apart! The oxygen (O) is the air Raed breathes. The hydrogen (H) floats away as a gas.
🚀 Real astronauts on the International Space Station make some of their air this way, using electricity and water!
